change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about this article. Fig. 7 does not correspond to its legend and text, and does not report an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the H460 siRNA migration result is unsupported; the paper's text makes exactly that migration claim. The notice also flags a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 blot and insufficient control detail for the transfection experiments, and says similarities with other groups' work call the validity and provenance of the results into question. The authors did not respond or could not be reached, so the issues are unresolved, and the notice is an expression of concern, not a retraction.
evaluation: Your Section 3 takes the H460 LSD1 knockdown result in the scratch assay of Lv et al. [12] as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration, and the notice says the figure does not report an LSD1 siRNA experiment so that result is not supported. Your Section 2 cites the same paper for higher LSD1 in tumour tissue and shorter survival; the notice names no issue with that data, but its general concern about validity and provenance may reach it, which is uncertain. The notice is an Expression of Concern about unresolved issues, and the impact on your draft is medium, mainly because the central rationale in Section 3 rests on the questioned result.
recommendation: In Section 3 the draft takes the H460 knockdown result of Lv et al. as the clearest indication that LSD1 is a driver of migration, but the notice says the figure does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the result statement is not supported. Hedge that wording, don't build Aim 2 on this result, and look for independent evidence. The notice is an Expression of Concern about unresolved issues, and it says similarities with other groups' work call the validity and provenance of the reported results into question. Hedge the Section 2 tissue and survival statement too, and cite the notice alongside the paper; if a retraction comes later, this assistant's tracking will raise a new alert.
